title: Wan2GP README
claims: The README lists video support for Wan 2.1/2.2 and derived models, MiniMax H3, LTX-2, Hunyuan Video 1/1.5, LongCat, Kandinsky, LTXV and MagiHuman.

For MiniMax H3 v12.42, the author says 5-6GB VRAM for 5s/124 frames and 8-9GB for 15s at 832x480; the page gives no GPU model, host RAM, disk throughput, cold/warm timing or peak host memory for those claims.
H3 FL2VA supports text, start/last frame and sliding windows; H3 Ref2VA supports image/video/audio references and does not support sliding windows. Full and pruned variants are listed.
v12.434 adds H3 W4A8 asymmetric INT8 checkpoints; the README says the 4-bit weights reduce checkpoint size/system RAM and INT8 activations use compatible NVIDIA kernels on RTX 30-series or newer.

The v12.434 entry documents First Block Cache and Sol-Attn. Sol-Attn requires BF16, Triton 3.6+ and the listed RTX 40/50, H100/H200 or B100/B200 hardware; the README gives expected gains but no L4/A100 timing.

resources.gpu: Unspecified NVIDIA for H3 claims; RTX 30+ for W4A8 claim; listed Sol-Attn devices exclude L4/A100
resources.steps: 15-20 minimum for H3 in v12.42; exact timing claim absent
resources.precision: H3 BF16 for Sol-Attn; W4A8 INT8; many quantized formats supported
resources.workflow: WanGP UI, headless queue, API, MCP
resources.version_scope: extreme2k fork snapshot v12.434, not canonical current release

measurement_scope: author runtime claims, not a controlled GPU benchmark
limitations: Do not treat generic VRAM claims as L4 or A100 qualification; actual H3 success and failure can depend on model variant, precision, host RAM, allocator and VAE path. Main provenance check: extreme2k/Wan2GP is a fork of deepbeepmeep/Wan2GP, last pushed 2026-08-07; its v12.434 snapshot must not be described as the current canonical release. See INF18.

title: Wan2GP CLI and performance reference
claims: CLI exposes transformer quantization, PyTorch compile, SDPA/Flash/Sage/Sage2 attention, profiles 1-5, VRAM preload, FP16, INT8 Quanto/ConvRot save and GPU selection.

Profile 4 is documented as sending model parts block-by-block so models larger than VRAM can run; Profile 4+ saves up to about 1GB VRAM at a slight slowdown; Profile 5 is the fail-safe for low RAM/VRAM.
The default MMGP VRAM allocator has a RAM-spill mode. The page records about 5.4GB saved for H3 1920x1088/241 frames and about 1.5GB for H3 1280x720/241 frames, with no wall-time or GPU model.

Reserved/pinned RAM defaults are documented as 40% on Windows and 60% on Linux; Smart Memory Pinning uses about 1-2GB reserved RAM. The docs say the allocator works on NVIDIA GPUs with PyTorch 2.3+ and the RAM allocator with PyTorch 2.6-2.15.
The same document gives author examples for compile, low-VRAM profile 4, TeaCache multipliers and fallback to SDPA/profile 4/FP16.

resources.gpu: NVIDIA; no exact GPU in allocator measurements

measurement_scope: author documentation examples; no controlled L4/A100 run
limitations: Profile and allocator behavior does not establish a fixed RAM requirement or transfer time for every model; RAM spill may finish a job but is documented as slower.

title: DiffSynth-Studio MiniMax-H3 model details
claims: The docs describe MiniMax-H3 as a video-plus-native-stereo-audio model up to 2K and 15s.

The NF4 quick start enables VRAM management and says it requires a minimum of 7GB VRAM; the shown configuration uses BF16 compute and CPU offload/onload for H3 transformer, text encoder, video VAE and audio VAE.
The reproducible example uses 480x832, 124 frames, 50 steps, seed 0 and writes a 24fps MP4 with 32kHz audio.
The model table lists FL2VA, Ref2VA and Retake, plus NF4, pruned, INT8 ConvRot, FP8 and LightX2V 4-step entries; FL2VA and Ref2VA partitions have different DiT and text encoder weights.

The docs say tiled VAE reduces VRAM with slight numerical error and small extra inference time; Comfy-Org INT8 weights are supported through the comfy-kitchen backend, which requires `diffsynth[quant]`.
References can be image, video, audio or video-audio; input frame lists must already be 24fps, and the pipeline does not resample them.
measurement_scope: official example and stated minimum VRAM, no target-GPU timing
limitations: 7GB is a framework claim under its VRAM manager, not proof of usable H3 quality, wall time, host RAM or disk capacity on L4/A100.

title: DiffSynth-Studio LTX-2 model details
claims: LTX-2 docs state VRAM management is enabled and the LTX-2.3 example can run with a minimum of 8GB VRAM.
The shown pipeline uses CPU offload/onload and a Gemma QAT text encoder, LTX-2.3 22B dev weights, spatial upscaler, and stage-2 distilled LoRA.
The example generates 1024x1536, 121 frames with a two-stage pipeline and writes video plus audio.

The model table lists one-stage, two-stage and distilled T2AV/I2AV, audio-to-video, retake, IC-LoRA and camera-control entries for LTX-2.3; LTX-2.5 rows include T2AV, I2AV, A2V, Retake, T2A and spatial upscaler entries.
The page does not provide L4/A100 wall time, peak VRAM, host RAM, disk throughput or cold/warm measurements.

resources.precision: BF16 compute/offload; Gemma QAT Q4_0 text encoder in example
resources.workflow: one/two-stage LTX audio-video pipeline, optional spatial upscale

measurement_scope: official example and stated minimum VRAM, no target-GPU timing
limitations: The minimum VRAM claim does not establish the cost of two-stage/upscale or audio VAE in the target Colab profiles.

title: MiniMax-H3 NF4 with DiffSynth-Studio on Google Colab
claims: The author tested DiffSynth-Studio/MiniMax-H3-NF4 with NF4 components, VRAM management and disk offload, and reports a successful Colab Pro G4 run at 480x832, 124 frames and 50 steps.

The same article reports a free Colab T4 with approximately 14.56GiB total GPU memory: 448x256/56f/12 steps OOM at attention; 320x192/39f/8 OOM at scaled_dot_product_attention; 320x192/22f/6 reached 50% then OOM at bitsandbytes NF4 dequantization; 288x160/22f/6 completed with VRAM_LIMIT_GB=9.0 and OFFLOAD_MODE=disk.
The author explicitly labels the final T4 video far from practical quality and separates running to completion from usable quality.
The notebook required additional `av` and `bitsandbytes` packages and saved the ModelScope cache to Google Drive; model files were described as large and downloads took minutes or more.
The article records GPU-memory growth across consecutive runs when video/audio tensors remain referenced and shows explicit garbage collection/empty_cache cleanup.

resources.gpu: Colab Pro G4 for 480x832 success; Colab Free T4 for failure/success ladder
resources.vram_gb: ~14.56 T4 total; 9.0 configured limit for final run
resources.precision: NF4 model components; BF16 compute; bitsandbytes
resources.workflow: Colab notebook -> DiffSynth pipeline -> disk/CPU/GPU offload -> MP4+audio

measurement_scope: firsthand Colab notebook/report; no wall time, host RAM peak or disk throughput
limitations: G4 and T4 are not L4; the report supports failure modes and a low-resource boundary, not target-band qualification or speed.

title: FastVideo compatibility matrix
claims: The matrix identifies registered model IDs and says they can be passed to VideoGenerator.from_pretrained; the displayed registry commit is 8d89f30d.
It lists Wan2.1, Wan2.2 TI2V-5B/A14B/S2V, LTX-2/2.3/2.5, Hunyuan, and MiniMax H3 with T2VA/FL2VA/Ref2VA workloads; H3 variants generate stereo audio.
FastH3 V1/V2 support is separate from base H3; Preview V1 is T2VA, while distilled Ref2VA PDD is a separate path.
The optimization table marks VSA/Sage/TeaCache support per model; registered models absent from the table are untested against those optimizations, not proven incompatible.
The document says Wan-VACE is not supported on main and LTX-2.5 official split/gated files need conversion to FastVideo component layout.
Full Sliding Tile Attention is archived on sta_do_not_delete and currently requires Hopper GPUs; TurboWan2.1 requires SLA_ATTN, RCM and guidance_scale=1.0.

resources.gpu: NVIDIA x86_64 CUDA 12.6/13.0; Hopper required for archived STA; no L4/A100 timing
resources.resolution: Model-specific: Wan2.2 TI2V 720P; LTX and H3 entries have separate recipe grids
resources.workflow: VideoGenerator Python API, basic examples, CLI/server recipes

measurement_scope: support/compatibility table, not a target-GPU performance benchmark
limitations: Support marks do not establish memory minimums or end-to-end MP4 success on L4/A100; absent optimization validation is unknown rather than incompatible.

title: FastVideo optimization and offloading docs
claims: FastVideo transformer FP8 quantization uses FP8 e4m3 for DiT linear layers. Hardware FP8 compute requires sm89+; GPUs older than sm89 automatically take a BF16 dequant path.
The docs list Wan2.1 as a runnable FP8 example and distinguish tensor granularity (faster/lower accuracy) from channel granularity (slower/higher accuracy).

torch.compile can compile eligible DiT submodules; text encoder and VAE are not compiled by the enable_torch_compile flag. The regional inference compile path has H3-specific guards and keeps unsupported VSA paths eager.
MiniMax-H3 VSA inference compile is limited to an inference-only sm100a tile-64 route; unsupported devices/legacy VSA keep the transformer eager with a warning.

Offloading docs list CPU offload, layerwise offload, text encoder/VAE offload and pin_cpu_memory defaults. H3 lazy_module_load loads components on first use and frees them after their last stage; h3_sequential_load loads Qwen3-VL, releases it, then loads DiT/VAEs.
The docs warn that unified-memory GB10/Apple devices disable host offload because host and accelerator share one pool; this is a device-specific exception.

resources.gpu: FP8 native compute sm89+; pre-sm89 BF16 fallback; H3 VSA compile sm100a only
resources.precision: FP8 e4m3 with BF16 dequant fallback below sm89
resources.workflow: Python VideoGenerator or fastvideo generate config

measurement_scope: official compatibility and runtime contract; no L4/A100 wall time
limitations: L4 is sm89 while A100 is sm80, but the docs alone do not establish that each model/loader will use the same fallback path or memory behavior on those cards.

title: FastH3 official blog and recipe page
claims: FastH3 Preview V1 is an open-weight 4-step sparse-distilled MiniMax-H3 T2VA model; it reuses H3 base text encoder, video VAE and audio VAE.
The recommended VSA/Data-Free checkpoint uses 90% sparse VSA, tile 64 and four DiT calls. Its reported speed claims are up to 14x on one NVIDIA Blackwell and under 13s for 15s 768p on 8xB200.
The official page says the reported speed/quality requires FastVideo VSA-H3; dense attention is not a drop-in substitute.
Preview V1 checkpoints support T2VA only. The page explicitly says first/last-frame conditioning was not used to train these students and Ref2VA needs a separate distilled checkpoint.

The maintained recipe page states FastH3 V2 is an 8-forward checkpoint, Preview V1 is 4-forward, CompactH3 is a 42-block NVFP4 checkpoint for one Blackwell GPU, and CUDA full H3 examples request four GPUs by default without claiming a memory minimum.

resources.gpu: Blackwell for published timing claims; CUDA recipe default 4 GPU without model/memory minimum
resources.precision: VSA sparse-distilled; CompactH3 NVFP4 Blackwell path

dependencies: CUDA or MLX for separate runtimes
measurement_scope: official model/release timing on Blackwell; not L4/A100
limitations: Do not apply Blackwell-only speed or NVFP4 claims to L4/A100; V1/V2 task contracts differ from base H3 and Ref2VA.

title: LightX2V MiniMax-H3 scripts and config
claims: The README describes H3 T2AV, I2AV, L2AV, FL2AV and Ref2AV tasks; the five ordinary scripts share a one-GPU BF16, model-CPU-offload config at 544x960 and 124 frames.

The checked JSON sets infer_steps=29, cpu_offload=true, offload_granularity=model, use_adaln_cache=true, text_encoder_cpu_offload=true, vae_cpu_offload=true, SageAttention2, SGL RMS and compile false.

The H3 CPU-offload path requires an AdaLN cache generated with the same model variant, steps and flow shifts; inference loads a matching cache strictly and does not silently fall back to online computation.
The README lists single-GPU Sol configs with 362 frames at 768x1344 and says compile configs set warmup=true; this is a config default, not a GPU result.
Quantized FP8/INT8/ConvRot DiT weights require dynamic LoRA application; merging a LoRA into quantized DiT weights is unsupported. FP8 VAE encoder modes require converted weights and SM120.

resources.gpu: One GPU config; no GPU model or target-band measurement stated
resources.precision: BF16 ordinary; FP8/INT8 quantized variants; SageAttention2/SGL
resources.workflow: bash task scripts, Python CLI, service/parallel scripts

measurement_scope: official config and task contract; no single L4/A100 timing
limitations: One-GPU config does not prove fit or speed on L4/A100; H3 544p/768p configs and quantized LoRA contracts must not be mixed.

title: LightX2V Wan2.1-14B beginner guide
claims: The guide exposes single-GPU, single-GPU-offload and multi-GPU scripts for Wan2.1 T2V/I2V, with 4-step distilled LoRA, merged LoRA and FP8 quantized variants.
On one H100, T2V BF16 was reported as 278.902019s/43,768MiB; distilled LoRA 31.365923s/44,438MiB; merged LoRA 25.794410s/44,418MiB; distilled+FP8 22.000187s/31,032MiB.
With model CPU offload, T2V BF16 was 319.019743s/34,932MiB; distilled LoRA 74.180393s/34,562MiB; merged LoRA 68.621963s/34,562MiB; distilled+FP8 58.921504s/21,290MiB.
The guide says VRAM was observed with watch nvidia-smi and gives no host RAM or disk throughput; resolution/frame/step details are not fully repeated beside these rows.

resources.precision: BF16 baseline; FP8 quantized distilled variant
resources.workflow: LightX2V bash scripts, single GPU or model CPU offload

title: Deploy MiniMax-H3 with Sol Engine on H100/A100
claims: The page evaluates MiniMax-H3 T2VA/I2VA/Ref2VA at 1344x768, 124 frames, about 5.2s at 24fps, 50 BF16 steps, batch 1.
The benchmark is warm after one warmup request, with same prompt/seed/model/resolution/topology for dense and full-opt; four A100 uses Ulysses-4 and no model offload.
On 4x A100, dense end-to-end is 217.32s and full-opt is 61.28s, a reported 3.55x speedup. Full-opt peak is 49,126MiB per A100.

A100 SM80 uses a portable Triton sparse-attention backend; H100 SM90 uses CuTe. Shared policy keeps first 10 steps and first two layers dense; Sol-Attn route density is 18.04% and FirstBlockCache reuse 67.35%.
The page explicitly states four GPUs and disabled offload, so the measurement is high-resource multi-GPU evidence.

resources.workflow: SGLang runtime logging, Sol Engine full-opt, Ulysses-4, no offload

measurement_scope: warm batch-1 four-A100 controlled same-prompt comparison
limitations: Cannot be divided into a single-A100 result; no A100 40GB, L4, host RAM or offload qualification is provided.

title: SGLang Diffusion MiniMax-H3 cookbook
claims: SGLang Diffusion serves MiniMax-H3 T2VA/FL2VA/Ref2VA and exposes native pipelines, `sglang generate`, `sglang serve` and an OpenAI-compatible path.

H3 weight support includes FP8/MXFP8, ConvRot INT8, W4A8/W4A4, NVFP4 and GGUF; the docs specify device/backend eligibility: NVFP4 requires compute capability 10.0+, W4A8/W4A4 require comfy-kitchen, and INT8 ConvRot uses JIT ops on CC9/10/12 while CC8.9 uses comfy-kitchen.
The documented 4090 recipe streams DiT/text encoder and leaves VAE out of layerwise offload because VAE decoder offload would re-stream about 9GiB on each of 167 decode tiles.

The docs report a 12GB hard-cap emulation at 864x480/124f/20 NFE: Recipe A with 32/48/64GB host measured 235/218/180s; Recipe B with 16GB VRAM cap and 116.7GB pinned host measured 120.92s. The page says these rows patch psutil and allocator caps, so they are not physical L4/A100 runs.
H3 torch.compile is opt-in and changes numerical output in the current path; the recommended lossless presets leave it disabled.

resources.gpu: RTX 4090 physical recipe; 12GB/16GB rows use hard allocator and psutil host emulation
resources.ram_gb: 32/48/64 physical/emulated for Recipe A; 116.7GB pinned for Recipe B
resources.workflow: sglang serve/generate, layerwise offload, optional Spectrum/Cache-DiT

measurement_scope: official cookbook; physical 4090 plus hard-cap/psutil host emulation
limitations: Not an L4 or A100 measurement. The host and allocator emulation explicitly limits transfer and capacity conclusions.

title: SGLang Cache-DiT diffusion acceleration docs
claims: SGLang integrates Cache-DiT and states an up-to-1.69x inference-speedup claim with minimal quality loss.
The document names DBCache, TaylorSeer, DMD Calibrator and SCM; it says Cache-DiT also ships SVDQuant W4A4 dynamic quantization that can combine with DBCache.
Cache-DiT is a per-request switch; requests with different settings do not share a batch. Warmup and residual threshold/SCM choices are explicit request/server settings.
The supported model list includes Wan2.1, Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo and MiniMax-H3 T2VA/FL2VA/Ref2VA.
measurement_scope: official speed claim and support list; no target-band run
limitations: The 1.69x claim is not a controlled L4/A100 result in this page; cache settings trade exactness/quality and must be checked per model.

title: vLLM-Omni diffusion features and supported model tables
claims: The video feature matrix lists Wan2.2, Wan2.2-S2V, LTX-2/2.3/2.5, SANA-Video-2B, HunyuanVideo-1.5, MiniMax-H3 and other video pipelines.

The MiniMax-H3 row marks FL2VA TeaCache, Cache-DiT, sequence parallel, DiT/TE tensor parallel, HSDP, layerwise CPU offload, VAE tile and DiT quantization as supported; CFG parallel and step execution are not marked supported in that row.

Wan2.2 supports Cache-DiT, sequence/CFG/tensor/pipeline parallel, HSDP, layerwise offload and VAE encode/decode tile; LTX-2/2.3 supports Cache-DiT, Ulysses, CFG/tensor parallel, HSDP, layerwise offload and VAE decode tile; LTX-2.5 has some unknown/restricted cells.
Quantization methods are listed as FP8, INT8 and GGUF transformer-only; CPU offload has module-wise and layerwise strategies, and multi-thread weight loading targets startup time.
The compatibility notes say TeaCache and Cache-DiT are not compatible, layerwise and module-wise CPU offload are not compatible, and step execution is not compatible with diffusion cache backends.

title: Wan2.2 TI2V-5B A100 80GB serving recipe
claims: The recipe qualifies one A100-SXM4-80GB for native 720p Wan2.2 TI2V-5B text-to-video and image-to-video without CPU offload or multi-GPU parallelism.
The contract is 1280x704, 121 frames, 24fps, 50 steps and seed 42 at a synchronous OpenAI-compatible Videos API endpoint; T2V omits input_reference and I2V uploads one image.
The host had 1TiB RAM and model loading used 21.2239GiB; the profile used BF16, native FlashAttention, eager mode and VAE tiling.
After warmup, T2V returned HTTP 200 in 288.267s with server peak 26,546MB and observed device peak 27,533MiB; I2V took 299.439s with 30,333MiB observed device peak.
ffprobe verified 1280x704, 121 frames, 24fps, 5.041667s MP4 for both outputs; the author reports full decode and visual inspection.

title: vLLM-Omni online text-to-video examples
claims: The examples support Wan2.1/2.2 T2V, LTX-2, Helios and SANA-Video 2B through `vllm serve --omni`; async `POST /v1/videos` stores a job and sync `POST /v1/videos/sync` is intended for benchmark/testing and returns `X-Inference-Time-S`.
The Wan examples expose flow_shift, boundary_ratio, guidance, frame count, fps, seed and an optional cache backend; generated files can be stored under a configurable local storage path.

The LTX-2 script reports H800 measurements for 480x768, 41 frames, 20 steps: eager baseline 10.3s; compile warm about 10.3s with first request +6s warmup; Ulysses4 about 10.3s; Cache-DiT 7.4s average and lossy; 4-GPU Ulysses4+Cache-DiT 4.7s average.
The same script labels compile as one-GPU and Cache-DiT as lossy; the best combo is explicitly four GPUs.

title: LightX2V MiniMax-H3 4xV100 benchmark
claims: The report measures native-FP16 MiniMax-H3 with LightX2V TP4 on four Tesla V100 PCIe 32GB cards, 256GiB host RAM and no swap; it uses a precomputed H3 text-conditioning tensor.

At 864x480/124f, fresh process load/merge is 25.11s, hot six-evaluation DiT is 49.73s, separate single-V100 video/audio VAE decode is 43.93s, and hot DiT plus fresh VAE is 93.66s; live text encoding is excluded.
At 1344x768/362f, the first evaluation OOMs; 1344x768/243f completes with 681.83s hot DiT and 32,072MiB per card.
The report separates load, hot DiT, VAE and fresh/two-phase timing and states model files were read from warm shared storage, not cold storage.

resources.workflow: LightX2V TP4, precomputed text conditioning, official H3 VAE decode

measurement_scope: firsthand high-resource multi-GPU benchmark with warm storage, precomputed text conditioning
limitations: V100 multi-GPU and excluded text encoder make this a timing decomposition/upper-bound failure reference, not L4 or single-A100 qualification.

title: Canonical Wan2GP README and repository provenance
claims: Canonical README lists v13.141 dated 2026-09-29 and model support including H3, LTX-2.3/2.5 and Wan2.1/2.2.
GitHub API reports canonical last push 2026-10-07; extreme2k/Wan2GP is its fork and was last pushed 2026-08-07.
Canonical Wan2GP itself historically forks Wan-Video/Wan2.1, so a fork flag alone is not evidence that a repository is invalid.
limitations: Repository/README version and support claims, not a specified-GPU runtime or quality benchmark.
